title: Feature Flags, Kill Switches, and Safe Operation Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies feature flags, kill switches, and safe operation?
options: Provide a nonblocking safe default and an audited control that preserves state while stopping harmful work.
Fetch every flag before first frame
questions.answer: Provide a nonblocking safe default and an audited control that preserves state while stopping harmful work.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: A kill switch eliminates the need for backwards-compatible server and database changes.
questions.explanation: Using a remotely fetched flag as the only defence against a crashing startup path fails when the app crashes before it can fetch the disabling value.

questions.prompt: What must happen when flag configuration cannot be fetched?
questions.answer: The app follows a predefined safe cached/default behaviour without blocking critical startup or losing durable state.
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
